headline: Continued Isla Express restaurant license hearing at 584 Smithfield Avenue to November 10; approved four event licenses.
summary: Neighbors on Smithfield Avenue spoke against the restaurant, citing parking, rodents, and disturbances. The owner, Judy Henriquez, said she was willing to meet with residents.
decisions: Approved the records of October 7, 2026 as prepared by the Clerk.
Approved the consent agenda by unanimous voice vote.
Approved first class victualling house license for Providence Express at 756 East Ave., by unanimous voice vote.
Approved beer and wine license for Burbage Theatre Company's Big Time Celebration on October 26, 2026, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved the Second Annual Little Mx. Burbage Halloqween Drag Night license, with food and alcohol, on October 31, 2026, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved one-day Christmas Market and outdoor alcohol expansion at 78 Carter Avenue on November 28, 2026, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved one-day corn hole tournament and alcohol expansion at 816 Main Street on October 24, 2026, by unanimous voice vote.
Continued the public hearing on Isla Express at 584 Smithfield Avenue and postponed the license to November 10, 2026, by unanimous voice vote.

382 
Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners 
October 21, 2026 
 
A regular session of the Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners was held Wednesday, 
October 21, 2026, at 7:01 p.m., in the Pawtucket Municipal Annex, City C ouncil Chambers, 
1st floor, 100 Freight Street, Pawtucket, RI. 
 
Present – President Mercer; Councilors Araujo, Coderre, Gregor, Moreno, Stachowiak and 
Wildenhain. 
 
Absent – Councilors Moran and Rubio. 
 
Chairperson Mercer presided.  
 
The reading of the records of October 7, 2026 wa s dispens ed with and the records were 
APPROVED as prepared by the Clerk. 
 
 
 
Upon motion made by Councilor Araujo, seconded by Councilor Moreno, the *Consent 
Agenda was APPROVED, on a unanimous voice vote. 
 
*THE FOLLOWING PETITION FOR LICENSE WAS APPROVED ON A UNANI MOUS 
VOICE VOTE: 
 
VICTUALLING HOUSE First Class New – 
 
Providence Express (Providence Express Inc.) 756 East Ave. LIC#VIC-26-23 
 
 
 
THE FOLLOWING PETITION FOR LICENSE S WAS APPROVED ON A UNANIMOUS 
VOICE VOTE: 
 
ENTERTAINMENT & CLASS F (Beer & Wine) –  
 
Petition of Burbage Theatre Company, for a license to conduct a Burbage Theatre Company’s 
Big Time Celebration – Fundraising Gala at 59 Blackstone Avenue to sell beer & wine on 
Monday, October 26, 2026, from 7:00 p.m. until 10:00 p.m. LIC#EVT-26-88 
 
 
 
THE FOLLOWING PETITION FOR LICENSE S WAS APPROVED ON A UNANIMOUS 
VOICE VOTE: 
 
ENTERTAINMENT & CLASS F-1 (Full Privilege) - 
 
Petition of Burbage Theatre Company, for a license to conduct the Second Annual Little Mx. 
Burbage Halloqween Drag Night, and to sell food and alcoholic beverages at 59 Blackstone 
Avenue, on Saturday, October 31, 2026, from 9:00 p.m. until 12:00 a.m. LIC#EVT-26-90 
 
 
 
THE FOLLOWING PETITION FOR LICENSE WAS APPROVED ON A UNANIMOUS 
VOICE VOTE: 
 
ENTERTAINMENT & EXPANSION OF PREMISE (One Day) – 
 
Petition of German American Cultural Society of RI, 78 Carter Avenue, for a license to 
conduct an indoor and outdoor Christmas Market and for a one -day expansion of their Class

from 12:00 p.m. until 5:00 p.m. LIC#EVT-26-91
383 
Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners 
October 21, 2026 
 
THE FOLLOWING PETITION FOR LICENSE WAS APPROVED ON A UNANIMOUS 
VOICE VOTE: 
 
ENTERTAINMENT & EXPANSION OF PREMISE (One Day) –  
 
Petition of Societe Jacques Cartier Cercle No. 4 , for license to conduct the Jacques Cartier 
Corn Hole Tournament and for a one -day expansion of their Class D Liquor License to serve 
food and alcoholic beverages at 816 Main Street, (outdoors) on Saturday, October 24, 2 026, 
from 11:00 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. LIC#EVT-26-89 
 
 
 
A PUBLIC HEARING ON THE FOLLOWING APPLICATION FOR A LICENSE, WHICH 
WAS ADVERTISED FOR A HEARING AT THIS TIME, WAS TAKEN UP: 
 
CLASS B (VICTUALLER) New –  
 
Isla Express (Isla Express LLC) 584 Smithfield Avenue, LIC#LQB-26-9® 
(Prev. 20/20 Hookah Lounge) 
 
Speaking in support was Judy Henriquez, 19 Earl Street, Lincoln, RI, applicant.  Also present 
was Giselle Pacheco, 19 Earl Street, Lincoln, RI. 
 
Ms. Henriquez stated that she has 25 years of experience in t he food service industry. She has 
owned and operated a restaurant in Providence for the past 10 years. 
 
The Pawtucket establishment will be more of a cafeteria  style, fast-food restaurant , not a 
lounge.   It has been operating for approximately three to four months 
.  
The hours will be Monday through Thursday: 9:00 a.m. to 7:00  or 8:00  p.m., Friday and 
Saturday: 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 a.m. and on Sunday they will have brunch until 7:00 p.m. 
 
The business has 10 parking spaces.  
 
Lunch is the busiest time of day.  The establishment has an open takeout window, indoor 
seating will be available for people who want to have a drink.  Customers will be permitted to 
have drinks with their meals; however, there will be no bar on the premises. 
 
 
Speaking in opposition was Taisha Long, 588 Smithfield Avenue, Pawtucket (via Zoom).  
 
Ms. Long stated that customers frequently park in and in front of her driveway and in front of 
her house. She also noted that tenants occupy some of the establishment’s 10 parking spaces, 
further limiting available parking. 
 
She stated that when she raised her concerns with the restaurant owner, she felt that her 
concerns were disregarded. She described the customers as rude and expressed concern that 
the situation would worsen if alcohol service we re permitted. She also stated that she had to 
contact the police regarding these issues. 
 
 
Speaking in opposition was Gabriella Colonette , 588 Smithfield Avenue , Pawtucket  (via 
Zoom).  
 
Ms. Colonette reported concerns similar to those raised by Taisha Long , stating that 
customers park in her driveway and that she has had to go to the restaurant to ask customers 
to move their vehicles. 
 
She expressed concern that allowing alcohol service could lead to increased disturbances and 
make the neighborhood rowdier.  She also reported problems with rodents and overflowing 
dumpsters, stating that these issues have caused significant stress.   Ms. Colonette opposed 
allowing the restaurant to remain open late due to the ongoing parking, sanitation, and 
neighborhood disturbance concerns.
384 
Pawtucket Board of License Commissioners 
October 21, 2026 
 
Speaking in opposition was Cynthia Diaz, 596 Smithfield Avenue, Pawtucket, (via Zoom). 
 
Ms. Diaz expressed that she lives in one of the newly constructed units.  S he noted that she 
already has to deal with issues involving a nearby bar and its intoxicated customers.   She 
doesn’t want another .  She is concerned about  belligerent customers, parking and rodent  
issues.  
 
A fourth neighborhood resident, whose name was unclear, spoke (via Zoom) in opposition to 
the application, stating that the neighborhood had experienced problems with a previous bar at 
the same location. She also expressed concerns regarding ongoing parking difficulties and 
rodent problems in the neighborhood. 
 
 
Ms. Henriquez stated that she owns the property and that the establishment is kept spotless 
and very clean. She said that her reviews on Google talk about the cleanliness of her 
establishment.  She denied that the rodent issues were caused by her business and noted that 
she had never experienced similar problems when operating her restaurant in Providence. She 
also stated that she had cleaned up the surrounding area and that none of the neighbors had 
contacted her directly to complain. 
 
Ms. Henriquez stated tha t the police had been called regarding a neighbor. She noted that 
signage directing customers to park in the rear of the property had been posted. 
 
She expressed her willingness to meet with neighborhood residents to discuss their concerns 
and emphasized that she intends to operate a family-friendly establishment. 
 
 
There were no other speakers.   The public hearing was closed. 
 
THE CHAIR RECOGNIZED COUNCILOR STACHOWIAK.   
 
Upon motion made by Councilor Stachowiak, seconded by Councilor Araujo, the hearing was 
CONTINUED and the following petition for license was POSTPONED until the meeting on 
November 10, 2026, on a unanimous voice vote. 
 
CLASS B (VICTUALLER) New –  
 
Isla Express (Isla Express LLC) 584 Smithfield Avenue, LIC#LQB-26-9® 
(Prev. 20/20 Hookah Lounge) 
 
 
 
Upon motion made by Councilor  Araujo, seconded by Councilor Moreno, the meeting was 
adjourned at 7:34 p.m.
